scope: Kyrgyz oymo and hand embroidery for a Kenius website background

sources.title: Киргизский национальный узор
sources.author: М. В. Рындин; редактор И. А. Орбели
sources.read: Selected descriptions: scan pages 28–34; plates X, XIII, XXV, XXVI–XXX; cover and title verified. Not a full-book reading.
sources.claim: The catalogue records motifs from nature, living creatures, plants, household objects, mythical imagery, and combinations; names depend on context.
sources.limitation: Historical terminology and interpretations are not a universal contemporary dictionary.

sources.title: Saima embroidery and tush-kiiz wall hanging
sources.author: Murat Suyunbaev / World Crafts Council Asia Pacific
sources.claim: Embroidered materials, ilme and basma stitches, named floral/animal motifs, three-sided tush-kiiz borders.
sources.limitation: Do not repeat its unquantified current-practitioner decline claim as a 2026 fact.

sources.title: Tush Kiiiz — Wall Decoration_Batken
sources.author: KyrgyzCraft / ICHCAP
sources.claim: Batken wall textiles and techniques ilme, ilmedos, basma, tuura saima, ters kayyk.
sources.limitation: Regional record, not a national exhaustive stitch classification.

sources.title: The Ethnographic Collection of the Gapar Aitiev Kyrgyz National Museum of Fine Arts
sources.author: Snezhana Atanova, with museum director and conservators
sources.type: Museum curator testimony and collection objects
sources.claim: Attributed early-20th-century tush-kiyiz, velvet and silk thread, three-sided border; embroidered clothing and bags.
sources.limitation: Museum objects are specific examples; arrangements are not a single rule for every region.

sources.title: World Quilts: Around the Home
sources.author: International Quilt Museum / University of Nebraska–Lincoln
sources.claim: Tush ki’iz horizontal format, embroidered or patchwork top and side panels.
sources.limitation: The collection includes regional and mixed-technique examples.

sources.title: Ala-kiyiz and Shyrdak: Art of Kyrgyz Traditional Felt Carpets
sources.author: UNESCO multimedia archive / CACSARC-kg / National Fine Art Museum
sources.claim: Ala-kiyiz and shyrdak are felt-carpet traditions.
sources.limitation: The embroidery study is not interchangeable with felt carpet production.

sources.title: Embroidery (tush kiyiz)
sources.author: Kyrgyzjer
sources.claim: Rounded embroidery motifs; radial and branching arrangements; chain-stitch texture.
sources.limitation: Corroborating context only; some regional and material claims are broad.

sources.title: Кыргызские орнаменты
sources.author: Open.kg
sources.claim: Single/double horn variants, kyial branching lines, S-shaped it kuiruk, regional naming differences.
sources.limitation: Unclear original author; do not treat as independent confirmation of historical interpretations.

confidence: High for craft distinction and documented names; moderate for grouping; no universal symbolic meanings asserted.
contradictions: A search-indexed AKI PDF labelled as ornament plates proved on visual inspection to be Bernshtam’s 1943 canal archaeology book. Excluded entirely.
Tush kiyiz placement and stitched central fields vary across sources; adopted composition as design inspiration, not a universal rule.
WCC felt-carpet page gives a UNESCO inscription date inconsistent with UNESCO itself; not used.
No reliable exhaustive count of Kyrgyz motifs or regional variants was established.

design.status: Original contemporary SVG interpretation, not a tracing or reproduction of an antique textile.
design.composition: Floral rosettes, leaves, S-curving sprigs, small geometric spacers; looped contour detail.
basis: Ryndin plate X: embroidery combinations and scrolling plant forms
Ryndin plate XXV: floral motif diversity
WCC and museum accounts of saima/tush kiyiz
Kyrgyzjer descriptions of radial and branching composition
design.choice: Floral embroidery family selected as the main website repeat. Animal, celestial, household and mythical motifs are studied, not all mixed into the live repeat.
